name: Projected Recursive Teaching Dimension
definition: The **Projected Recursive Teaching Dimension** of $\mathcal{H}$ is $\max_{S\subseteq X}\mathrm{RTD}(\mathcal{H}_{|S})$: the largest recursive teaching dimension among all coordinate projections of $\mathcal{H}$.
graph_summary: Largest recursive teaching dimension among coordinate projections.
origin_references: The projection-monotone variant $\mathrm{RTD}^*$ is introduced and studied in \cite{doliwa2014recursive}.

monotonic.proof: For every projection, a subfamily projects to a subfamily. Recursive teaching dimension is subfamily-monotonic, so maximizing it over all projections preserves the inequality.

p_monotonic.proof: A projection of a projection is a projection. Therefore every recursive-teaching value included in $\mathrm{RTD}^p(\mathcal H_{|S})$ is among the values maximized in $\mathrm{RTD}^p(\mathcal H)$.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Counterexample to strict c-monotonicity: $\mathcal H=\{000,001,011,100\}$ has projected recursive teaching dimension 1, and conditioning the third coordinate gives two fibres that both still have projected recursive teaching dimension 1.
